items.followUp: State Newton’s first law of motion and explain how it describes inertia.

rubric.why: The answer must state both what a body does and what can change that state.
rubric.description: States that a body remains at rest or continues in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by an external force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the unchanged state and 1 mark for the external-force condition.

modelAnswer: A body remains at rest or continues to move with uniform velocity in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
This tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of rest or motion is called inertia.

items.followUp: Define the moment arm of a force and write the formula for the moment of force.

rubric.why: This identifies torque as the turning effect of a force and its relevant distance.
rubric.description: Defines torque as the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis.

rubric.why: The formula must relate torque to force and the perpendicular distance from the pivot.
rubric.description: Gives the mathematical formula for torque.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula, with the distance identified as perpendicular to the force’s line of action.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis.
Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot.
τ = F × d

items.followUp: State the Principle of Moments for a body in equilibrium and give one example of its use.

rubric.why: The principle requires the two opposite senses of rotation to balance.
rubric.description: States that, for a body in equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equality of clockwise and anticlockwise moments in equilibrium.

rubric.why: Moments must be compared about the same point, and the answer should convey their balancing effect.
rubric.description: Explains that the moments are taken about the same point and balance one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of the balance about a common point.

modelAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a point is equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point.
Thus, the turning effects balance and the body does not rotate.

items.followUp: Define efficiency and write its formula as a percentage.

rubric.why: Efficiency compares the useful output with the total input.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as the ratio of useful output work to total input work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The formula must include the ratio and the factor of 100 for percentage efficiency.
rubric.description: Writes the formula for percentage efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output work to total input work.
Efficiency = (useful output work ÷ total input work) × 100%

items.followUp: Define power and state the value of one watt in terms of joules and seconds.

rubric.why: Power describes how quickly work is done.
rubric.description: Defines power as the rate of doing work.

rubric.why: One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating 1 W = 1 J/s or its equivalent in words.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work.
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.
1 W = 1 J/s

items.followUp: Define density and write its formula using mass and volume.

rubric.why: Density is mass per unit volume.
rubric.description: Defines density as mass per unit volume.

rubric.why: The formula must correctly relate density, mass, and volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
Density = mass ÷ volume
ρ = m/V

items.followUp: A lamp hangs at rest from two vertical strings with tensions of 5.2 N and 6.1 N. Find its weight.

rubric.why: The tensions must be correctly identified as the given upward forces.
rubric.description: Identifies the given tensions in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating both tensions.

rubric.why: The frame is at rest, so its weight balances the total upward tension.
rubric.description: Uses equilibrium to relate the weight to the two tensions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the weight equals the sum of the tensions.

rubric.why: This is the correct equation and substitution.
rubric.description: Substitutes both tension values into the weight equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution.

rubric.why: The required result is the sum of the two tensions, with a force unit.
rubric.description: Calculates and states the picture frame’s weight with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct answer with unit; award 1 mark if the numerical result is correct but the unit is missing.

modelAnswer: Given: T₁ = 3.8 N, T₂ = 4.4 N
Since the picture frame is at rest, it is in equilibrium.
Formula: W = T₁ + T₂
Substitution: W = 3.8 N + 4.4 N
Answer: W = 8.2 N

items.followUp: Derive the expression for pressure at a depth h in a liquid of density ρ.

rubric.why: The derivation starts with the definition of pressure.
rubric.description: States pressure as force per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or formula.

rubric.why: The liquid column has volume Ah and mass equal to density times volume.
rubric.description: Finds the volume and mass of the liquid column above the area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly relating the column’s volume or mass to A, h, and ρ.

rubric.why: The pressure-producing force is the weight of the liquid column.
rubric.description: Obtains the weight of the liquid column as its force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct expression for the column’s weight.

rubric.why: Dividing the weight by area gives the required liquid-pressure formula.
rubric.description: Derives the final expression for pressure at depth h.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final formula.

modelAnswer: Consider a liquid column of height h and cross-sectional area A.
Volume of the column = Ah.
If the liquid density is ρ, mass of the column = ρ × Ah = ρAh.
Weight of the column, F = mg = ρAhg.
Pressure, P = force ÷ area = F/A.
P = ρAhg/A.
Therefore, P = ρgh.
